editor_note: The three rewritten entries (40, 41, 44) keep the meaning: the 10% / 80–90% / approx. 15% figures, the widths 9 and 60, the 10- and 51-qubit totals and the calibration caveat all match the English. There are three small issues, all in entries 41 and 44. Entry 41 renders "non-trivial success probability" as 「自明ではない成功確率」, a calque of the math sense; 「無視できない成功確率」 is the natural wording. Both new entries also use 「隠しビット列」 where the rest of the page uses 「隠されたビット列」, and they write half-width parentheses (合計10量子ビット) where the rest of the page uses full-width （）.

examples.suggested: Orbitは幅が60に近づいても無視できない成功確率を維持し
examples.why: 「自明ではない」 is the math sense of non-trivial ("not obvious"). Here the English means a meaningfully nonzero probability, so the phrase reads as a calque.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English. Entry 72 keeps the control and target the right way round (Qを制御、自分のQubitをターゲットとするCNOT Gate, then the Hadamard on Q), and entry 73 renders "Because A and Q are in the same location, let us group…" as AとQは同じ場所にあるため、…測定結果に従って上記の項をまとめましょう, with nothing added or lost.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 53 is accurate: the seed_transpiler advice and the link to the Options list are both correct. In entry 87 the last tip drops "your own", so 「制約付き二値最適化問題に対して…試し」 no longer tells the reader to try the options on their own problem. In entry 78, 「ここでは最初の解のみを、変数名で指定して考慮します」 is a stiff calque of "addressed by variable name"; a native editor would write that the first solution is looked up by variable name.

examples.source: Experiment with the algorithm options (...) on your own constrained binary optimization problem to assess their impact on solution quality and runtime.
examples.translation: 制約付き二値最適化問題に対してアルゴリズムのオプション(...)を試し、解の質と実行時間への影響を評価してください。

examples.why: The translation drops the qualifier "your own", so the tip no longer invites readers to apply the options to their own problem. It loses part of the encouragement in the English.

examples.source: Only the first solution is considered here, addressed by variable name.
examples.translation: ここでは最初の解のみを、変数名で指定して考慮します。
examples.suggested: ここでは最初の解のみを扱い、各値には変数名でアクセスします。
examples.why: 「変数名で指定して考慮します」 is a calque and reads stiffly. The English means the solution's values are looked up by variable name, and a native writer would say that directly.

editor_note: Entry 60 keeps the meaning and keeps "Qiskit Function" in English, as the house style requires, so it would not mislead a learner. Its modifier chain reads awkwardly, though. "Quantum ElementsによるQiskit FunctionのOrbit" uses の to express the English appositive "Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements", so it reads as if Orbit belongs to a Qiskit Function. "Quantum Elementsによる" could also be read as modifying the whole benchmark. A native editor would use であるOrbit, for example "Quantum ElementsのQiskit FunctionであるOrbitを用いたQFTプロセス忠実度のベンチマーク", which also matches the "Q-CTRLのQiskit Functions" pattern in entry 57.

examples.source: Benchmark QFT process fidelity with Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements
examples.translation: Quantum ElementsによるQiskit FunctionのOrbitを用いたQFTプロセス忠実度のベンチマーク
examples.suggested: Quantum ElementsのQiskit FunctionであるOrbitを用いたQFTプロセス忠実度のベンチマーク
examples.why: Using の for the appositive ('Qiskit FunctionのOrbit') makes Orbit sound like part of a Qiskit Function, and 'Quantum Elementsによる' can be read as modifying the whole benchmark. であるOrbit is the natural way to say 'Orbit, a Qiskit Function' and avoids both readings.

editor_note: Entry 12 is faithful and reads naturally: frustration→フラストレーション, the parenthetical (例えば三角形配置において) is kept, "compounded globally" becomes 系全体で積み重なり, and "web of conflicting constraints" becomes 互いに矛盾する制約が複雑に絡み合った状態, with no drift in meaning.

None of the 23 rewritten entries misleads a learner. The O(n^2)-versus-O(n) argument in [17], the partitioning and PUB counts in [4], [31], [32] and [49], and the caveat on MEM-adjusted counts in [51] all match the English. Entry [51] has a corrupted character: '子Runtimeジョブ��ID' should read '子RuntimeジョブのID'. Entry [67] moves the location of the definitions: 'セットアップセクションの上部' means 'the top part of the Setup section', but the English says the Setup section is near the top of the page. Smaller issues: 'transpiler' appears as both 'トランスパイラー' ([33]) and 'トランスパイラ' ([42], [56]), and [21] says '例' twice in the same phrase.

examples.why: The text contains corrupted replacement characters (likely a broken 'の'), and readers will see them on the rendered page.
